Writing

Stories from the field

Features and articles written for CETRAD, turning research and community voices into stories people actually want to read.

Water and Gender

In water-scarce regions of Kenya, women often walk miles for a basic human right: clean water. This feature explores how CETRAD is bridging gender and water access through an Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) approach rooted in equity, policy reform, and community empowerment.

Through storytelling and stakeholder voices, the piece makes the case for gender-inclusive water governance — the kind that uplifts women, transforms households, and strengthens climate resilience.

Read the full story

Gums and Resins for Sustainable Livelihoods

This story follows CETRAD's landscape restoration work in Laikipia and its ripple effect on rural livelihoods. I looked at how tree planting, paired with training and long-term land-use planning, can create sustainable income while restoring degraded environments.

It blends storytelling with technical detail to make nature-based solutions feel relatable — part of a digital series on restoration and community empowerment.

Read the full story

Reviving Gambella Wetland

CETRAD partnered with the Wyss Academy for Nature to restore the degraded Gambella Wetland, once under severe threat from encroachment and resource depletion. Over 6,000 indigenous trees went into the ground, alongside weirs, troughs, and kiosks that gave households and livestock new water sources.

Beyond the ecology, the project handed facilities to local users and brought landowners, conservationists, and officials together through a "Coalition for Change" — proof that restoration works best when the community owns it.

Read the full story

Growing More Than Trees

In Gambella, twenty young people from the Enlite Youth Group are taking restoration into their own hands — building a community-run tree nursery with a target of 100,000 seedlings. Led by Racho Ibrahim and supported by CETRAD, they're learning everything from seed selection to seedling care.

It's a story about what happens when young people aren't just invited to participate in conservation, but given the tools to lead it.

Visual design

Design & branded assets

I design for print and digital alike, using Adobe Illustrator and Canva to turn technical material into something people actually want to look at, while keeping every asset consistent with the brand behind it.

  • High-resolution event banners built around ecological themes and partner branding
  • Teardrop, feather flag, and roll-up banners for trainings and exhibitions
  • Infographics simplifying complex topics — IWRM, climate adaptation, land restoration — for social media and reports
  • Trifold brochures for field distribution and stakeholder meetings
  • A quarterly newsletter, designed cover to cover
